compendium.title: Compendium
compendium.lead: Short definitions students reach for most often. The full glossary stays in the mobile course repo.

definition: Command Query Responsibility Segregation — a pattern that separates writes (Commands) from reads (Queries).
A request that changes system state (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE). Usually returns an id or status.
A request to read data. It does not change application or database state.
A .NET Mediator library: you send a Request and it reaches a Handler through a pipeline.
An HTTP resource style for APIs — endpoints returning JSON, e.g. GET /items, POST /items.
Service containers: SQL Server, API, and dependencies start from the same docker-compose in the lab.
A .NET ORM (EF Core) that maps C# objects to SQL tables and handles migrations.
React for iOS and Android: one TypeScript codebase, two native apps.
JavaScript with types. Errors show up in the editor before they hit runtime.
Create, Read, Update, Delete — basic data operations, usually mapped to HTTP methods.
Checking input before the handler — in class: FluentValidation and a MediatR pipeline Behavior.
Splitting large lists into pages (PageNumber, PageSize) on the API and in the mobile client.

notes.title: Notes

items.title: Why CQRS shows up early in the lab
items.summary: How to separate Commands from Queries before the app grows.
body: On the mobile track CQRS appears early so students do not mix writes and reads in one service.
Start with GetAllItems and CreateItem — the Query vs Command difference is clear without heavy theory.
The full walkthrough is in lesson 3; lab code lives in PMAB2026Zaoczki.

items.title: Docker before the first API call
items.summary: A database container saves an hour of fighting local SQL Server.
body: Start the docker-compose from lesson 4 before wiring React Native to the API.
On the Android emulator localhost is not your laptop — check the host IP or use adb reverse.
The same containers return in the MVC course for the Company and Mine1 database.

items.title: Company and Mine1 — what is what
items.summary: Two MVC projects in one summer-course repository.
body: Company is the entry point: ASP.NET MVC structure and the first business scenario.
Mine1 extends the same stack with the next use case — do not start from scratch.
